title: Sparsity Curse: Understanding RLVR Model Parameter Space from Model Merging

problem.claim: The paper investigates whether the sparse parameter updates induced by RLVR make RLVR models more amenable to model merging.

gap.claim: Standard merging methods suffer severe degradation on RLVR models because their sparse updates are spread apart in parameter space and form near-orthogonal shortcuts.

contributions.claim: The paper identifies a sparsity curse in which RLVR updates are far apart in parameter space, making aggregation inherently fragile.
The paper proposes Sensitivity-aware Resolving Merging (SAR-Merging), which uses Fisher Information-based sensitivity arbitration followed by magnitude-aware sparsification and rescaling.
Experiments on mathematical and coding benchmarks report that SAR-Merging substantially outperforms existing merging methods for RLVR models.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present SAR-Merging as a merging recipe tailored to the unique structure of RLVR parameter spaces.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that RLVR has surpassed SFT in eliciting reasoning intelligence and resisting catastrophic forgetting.
The authors report severe degradation of RLVR models under standard merging methods.
The authors report substantial SAR-Merging gains on mathematical and coding benchmarks, including single-task enhancement and multi-capability fusion.

narrative_sequence.summary: RLVR is described as a powerful post-training paradigm, and its updates are reported to be highly sparse and off-principal compared with SFT.
The reported sparsity motivates examining whether RLVR models are more amenable to model merging as a scalable, training-free aggregation path.

The paper reports the opposite: sparse RLVR updates are farther apart and near-orthogonal, making aggregation fragile, possibly because of RL optimization stochasticity and diverse reasoning patterns.
The authors characterize the failure mechanism and introduce SAR-Merging with sensitivity arbitration, sparsification, and rescaling.
Experiments on mathematical and coding benchmarks report improved single-task enhancement and multi-capability fusion over existing merging methods.

source_observation.claim: Parameter-update sparsity does not necessarily improve mergeability; sparse updates may instead be distant and near-orthogonal.

interpretation.claim: The geometry and alignment of updates can matter more than sparsity alone when combining independently trained models.

application.claim: Model-combination methods should inspect update geometry and resolve sensitivity conflicts before sparsifying or rescaling updates.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this lesson generalizes beyond RLVR models or the reported mathematical and coding benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the mathematical and coding datasets, benchmark metrics, or model configurations.
The abstract does not identify the existing merging baselines or quantify the reported improvements.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or independent verification of the reported mechanism.
